title: Value Basis for the Loan-to-Value Cap by Deal Type
content:
# Underwriting note: the value basis behind the loan-to-value cap

For a GAP balance line under the Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda, the loan-to-value cap amount is the tier's loan-to-value cap percentage times the cap basis, rounded half up to the cent. The cap basis turns on the deal type and the cash price of the waiver's own purchase deal, as recorded on its Vehicle Purchase Agreements record:

| Waiver's purchase deal | Cap basis |
|---|---|
| Used Vehicle Retail Purchase or Value Line Used Vehicle Purchase, with a cash price below the vehicle value basis recorded on the waiver | the deal's cash price |
| Certified Pre-Owned Vehicle Purchase | the vehicle value basis recorded on the waiver plus 1,000.00 (USD 1000.00) |
| Any other deal, or a used or value-line deal whose cash price equals or exceeds the vehicle value basis | the vehicle value basis recorded on the waiver |

The cash price is the agreed selling price of the vehicle on the deal, before the documentary fee, government fees, taxes, trade-in and deposits.

### Worked cases (hypothetical figures)

- **Used Vehicle Retail Purchase, cash price 17,950.00, vehicle value basis 18,600.00, cap percentage 140 percent.** The cash price is below the value basis, so the cap basis is 17,950.00 and the cap amount is 25,130.00. Had the cash price been 18,600.00 or more, the cap basis would have been 18,600.00 and the cap amount 26,040.00.
- **Certified Pre-Owned Vehicle Purchase, vehicle value basis 22,300.00, cap percentage 125 percent.** The cap basis is 23,300.00 and the cap amount is 29,125.00.
- **New Vehicle Retail Purchase, vehicle value basis 41,233.00, cap percentage 175 percent.** The cap basis is 41,233.00 and the cap amount is 72,157.75.
